previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 2 diabetes and a recent hospitalization for nausea and acute kidney injury was readmitted with fever, severe crampy abdominal pain, and watery diarrhea. The infectious workup was negative, and symptoms resolved quickly, but persistent nausea and inability to tolerate food raised concern for gastroparesis. A gastric emptying study confirmed delayed gastric emptying. She was managed with high-dose ondansetron, dietary modifications, and discontinuation of labetalol due to bradycardia. She advanced to a full diet, had constipation resolved with laxatives, and was discharged home in improved condition with a lactose-free diet and follow-up plan.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ with a medical history of DM2 and recent diagnosis of 
gastroparesis who presents to ED with nausea, early satiety, 
epigastric abdominal pain, weight loss consistent with 
gastroparesis found to be relatively hypotensive with acute 
renal failure. 
.
#Gastroparesis. The patient was continued on metoclopramide 
(renal dosing) to promote gastric emptying and started on zofran 
for nausea.  Abdominal discomfort was minimal at presentation so 
an NGT was not necessary. Her diet was slowly advanced from 
clear liquids to solids. 
.
Hypotension.  The patient was noted to be relatively hypotensive 
with a blood pressure of 90/50 in the ED but this improved to 
106/65 after fluid bolus. On the floor her systolic blood 
pressure was initially in the high ___, with similar response to 
IVF bolus. Her anti-hypertensives were held during admission. 
.
#Acute renal failure. The etiology was most likely pre-renal 
secodary to dehydration in the setting of poor po intake. Her 
serum creatinine improved significantly with IV fluids and was 
approaching baseline at discharge. Her ACE-I was held in the 
setting of acute renal dysfunction. 
.
#Diabetes. Her oral agents were held in the setting of poor po 
intake and she was started on an insulin sliding scale. She 
demonstrated good blood sugar control during the 
hospitalization.
.

your systolic BP (top number) is > 160 on home monitoring.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  Left-sided abdominal pain.  Query diverticulitis.

COMPARISON:  ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Multiple MDCT axial images were obtained from the base of the
lungs through the proximal thighs after the uneventful administration of 100
cc of Visipaque intravenously.  Multiplanar reformats were derived.

CT OF THE ABDOMEN WITH INTRAVENOUS CONTRAST:  In the visualized thorax, the
heart is normal in size, without pericardial effusion.  There is a nodule in
the right middle lobe (series 2, image 4), measuring approximately 2 mm and
stable from ___.  No pulmonary mass, pleural effusion, or pneumothorax is
seen.  There is a small hiatal hernia (series 2, image 14).

In the abdomen, the liver, pancreas, spleen, and adrenals appear normal. 
There is no intra- or extra-hepatic bile duct dilatation.  There has been a
cholecystectomy.  Kidneys symmetrically take up and excrete contrast.  Again
seen is an approximately 2.4 cm diameter hypodensity, attenuating, equivalent
to simple fluid, in the lateral aspect of the posterior right kidney, likely a
simple cyst.  Incidental note is made of a splenule.  Abdominal loops of bowel
appear normal.  There is no abnormal dilatation or pericolonic fat stranding. 
There is no free fluid, free air, or pathologic lymphadenopathy.  The
abdominal aorta is normal in caliber and course.

CT OF THE PELVIS WITH INTRAVENOUS CONTRAST:  Pelvic loops of bowel appear
normal.  There is no pronounced pericolonic fat stranding.  The bladder
appears normal.  The patient is status post hysterectomy and bilateral
salpingo-oophorectomy.  A calcified oval structure in the mid pelvis is
unchanged from prior and may represent a calcified hematoma or duplication
cyst.  There are numerous inguinal lymph nodes, but no pathologic enlargement.
There is no significant free fluid in the pelvis.

MUSCULOSKELETAL:  No suspicious osteolytic or osteoblastic lesions are seen. 
Mild degenerative changes are seen at numerous levels of the spine and at the
sacroiliac on right.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No CT findings to explain the patient's left lower quadrant pain.
2.  Stable right middle lobe pulmonary nodule, for which further
characterization is not needed.
3.  Small hiatal hernia.
4.  Unchanged rim calcified structure in the mid pelvis that may represent a
duplication cyst or calcified hematoma.
